exposure: intermittently absent end-diastolic umbilical artery Doppler flow
persistently absent end-diastolic umbilical artery Doppler flow
cohort: 137 pregnancies diagnosed with either intermittently absent end-diastolic umbilical artery Doppler flow (n=38) or persistently absent flow (n=99).
finding: Pregnancies with intermittently absent end-diastolic umbilical artery Doppler flow had a significantly longer latency from diagnosis to delivery, higher gestational age at delivery, and improved Apgar scores compared to those with persistently absent flow, suggesting it is a less severe form of placental insufficiency.
